unresolved_should_improve.claim:
The revision deletes two pieces of the Weed portrait:
- 'Mistake or not, Mr. Weed soon got into his hands the threads of management...'
- 'confidence was becoming the rarest' flower of education.
Weed now writes to the Times, which the Legation calls the amateur's mistake, and the text moves straight to praise and the little-dog devotion with no stated cause.
unresolved_should_improve.counterevidence: 'A complete American education in himself' and the unselfishness paragraph partly imply his effectiveness.

evidence.quote: into his hands the threads of management, and did quietly and smoothly
flowers in the garden of education, confidence was becoming the rarest;
Mistake or not, Mr. Weed soon got into his hands the threads of management
he wrote letters to the London Times. Thurlow Weed was a complete American education in himself. Before Mr. Weed went away, young Adams followed him about

unresolved_should_improve.minimal_repair: Restore 'Mistake or not, Mr. Weed soon got into his hands the threads of management.' Optionally prefix the little-dog sentence with 'Confidence was becoming the rarest flower of education; but'.
unresolved_should_improve.plan_relation: Essential lists Weed first seen writing to the Times; the payoff is implied by that framing.
unresolved_should_improve.reader_effect: The joke depends on the expert Legation being wrong about the amateur. Losing 'confidence' also cuts the link between Weed and the chapter's governing question of trust.
unresolved_should_improve.title: Weed's 'invariable mistake' left without its ironic payoff; confidence motif cut

unresolved_should_improve.claim: The revision cuts 'Earl Russell never disavowed Gladstone, although Lord Palmerston and Sir George Cornewall Lewis instantly did so.' That sentence is the student's evidence for his conclusion about Russell's intent.
unresolved_should_improve.counterevidence: Palmerston's repudiation via Lewis survives in paragraph 24, so half of the contrast remains.

Earl Russell never disavowed Gladstone, although Lord Palmerston and Sir George Cornewall Lewis instantly did so.
Mr. Gladstone's speech had been drawn out by Russell's own policy of intervention. As far as the curious student could penetrate the mystery, Gladstone exactly expressed Earl Russell's intent.

unresolved_should_improve.minimal_repair: Reinsert the one sentence before 'As far as the curious student could penetrate'.
unresolved_should_improve.plan_relation: Supports essential points (Palmerston has Lewis repudiate; Russell's explanation of Gladstone).
unresolved_should_improve.reader_effect: The verdict now rests only on 'drawn out by Russell's own policy'. The pointed contrast between Palmerston repudiating Gladstone and Russell staying silent is lost.
unresolved_should_improve.title: Key support for 'Gladstone exactly expressed Earl Russell's intent' removed

unresolved_should_improve.claim:
The revision drops two things from the first draft:
- Russell's biographer's account of the 23 October Cabinet.
- 'The Duke of Newcastle and Sir George Grey joined Granville in opposition.'
This leaves 'As far as known, Russell and Gladstone stood alone' with no stated basis.
unresolved_should_improve.counterevidence: The refusal itself and its timing relative to the 'Yes!' remain clear.

had asked the Cabinet to intervene, and that the Cabinet had refused. As far as known, Russell and Gladstone stood alone.
Pam., Johnny, and Gladstone would be in favor of it, and probably Newcastle.

unresolved_should_improve.minimal_repair: Restore 'Russell's biographer said the Cabinet assembled on October 23; the Duke of Newcastle and Sir George Grey joined Granville in opposition.'
unresolved_should_improve.plan_relation: Essential: 'Meanwhile the Cabinet had rejected his proposal that day.'
unresolved_should_improve.reader_effect: The chapter's irony depends on published documents arriving decades later, and the hedge 'As far as known' now floats unsourced. The Newcastle reversal is also lost: Granville had guessed 'probably Newcastle' would favor recognition.
unresolved_should_improve.title: Cabinet refusal loses its documentary source and named opponents

unresolved_should_improve.claim:
The revision cuts two parts of the build:
- 'If education had the smallest value, it should have shown its force in Gladstone, who was educated beyond all record...'
- The deliberate-reflection sentence and the 7 October morning diary entry.
So 'From him... the poor student could safely learn' and 'mature fruit of his long study' carry less weight.
unresolved_should_improve.counterevidence: 'Reflected on the subject for a fortnight' and 'deliberately pronounced' still signal premeditation; the finance-sanity premise survives.

it was the result of deep reflection pursued to the last moment.

reflected on the subject for a fortnight, until October 7, when he was to speak at a great dinner at Newcastle. That evening at dinner, as the mature fruit of his long study

unresolved_should_improve.minimal_repair: Restore the 'educated beyond all record' sentence in paragraph 20, and 'This decision was no sudden impulse' plus the one-line diary quotation in paragraph 21.
unresolved_should_improve.plan_relation: Essential: the Newcastle speech was 'reached after deliberate reflection'.
unresolved_should_improve.reader_effect: The chapter's education irony depends on the best-educated statesman being the worst teacher. The diary was the documentary proof that the speech was premeditated, which the plan marks as essential.
unresolved_should_improve.title: Gladstone set-piece loses its education premise and morning-diary evidence

unresolved_should_improve.claim: The plan says to compress the complexity aside to one sentence. The revision deletes it, including the first draft's 'Palmerston, Russell, and Gladstone deceived only by their simplicity.' The portraits now jump to Russell's want of good faith, and 'Palmerston was simple' arrives without the frame it answers.
unresolved_should_improve.counterevidence: Each portrait still stands on its own.

evidence.quote: Surely no one would believe that complexity was the trait that confused

if he learned such a lesson wrong. The only point in Russell's character about which the student thought no doubt to be possible was its want of good faith.

unresolved_should_improve.minimal_repair: Reinsert the first draft's single sentence after 'learned such a lesson wrong'.
unresolved_should_improve.plan_relation: Optional item said 'compress into one sentence'; full removal exceeds the plan.
unresolved_should_improve.reader_effect: The organizing paradox of the three portraits, deception through simplicity rather than complexity, disappears. The 'simple' Palmerston and the Gladstone 'sum of contradictions' lose their contrast.
unresolved_should_improve.title: 'Simplicity' frame cut entirely instead of compressed

unresolved_should_improve.counterevidence: 013 attributes the line to Gladstone's plea, so it remains intelligible there.
